is_anopheles.evidence: Indoor-resting mosquitoes of the Anopheles funestus group (An. funestus s.s. and An. rivulorum) were collected along Lake Kariba in southern Zambia (page 91).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No target resistance markers were genotyped. The authors state on page 95: 'resources were limited to perform molecular genotyping to characterize resistance mechanisms in the populations of An. funestus in the study areas.'

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No resistance marker genotyping was performed, so no genotype or allele counts are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Field collections of adult Anopheles mosquitoes were conducted in Southern Province, Zambia between April and May 2015 and reared to F1 for bioassays (pages 91-92).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research paper evaluating insecticide susceptibility, PBO synergism, and Plasmodium sporozoite infection in field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from six specific sites in Sinazongwe and Siavonga districts of Southern Province, Zambia: Buleyamalima, GVDC, Chiyabi, Sikaneka, Siatwinda, and Manchanvwa (pages 91-94, Figure 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted between April 2015 and May 2015 (page 91).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study was part of an MDA trial conducted in Southern Province, Zambia, with direct field collections performed by the study team.

supplement.evidence: The only supplemental file referenced is Supplemental Table S1 describing agricultural insecticides used in the study areas; no genotype data was gathered or withheld.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated susceptibility to deltamethrin, bendiocarb, pirimiphos-methyl, and DDT, as well as PBO synergism and sporozoite rates, in F1 Anopheles funestus s.l. from southern Zambia in 2015. However, no molecular resistance marker genotyping was performed.
exclusion_reasons: No target insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped in the mosquito populations.
